items.title: Genshin Impact devs' new action game Nodusfall feels like Elden Ring Nightreign at home, but don't write it off yet
items.summary: Going hands-on with Nodusfall at Gamescom 2026
items.content:
Going hands-on with Nodusfall at Gamescom 2026

(Image credit: HoYoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nodusfall does not look like your typical Hoyoverse game. Distinctly lacking in bright colors and bubbly anime-style characters, it's hard to believe that this gloomy, intense PvE action game comes from the same studio behind Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail. But after a brief hands-on session with the game, I'm already eager to dive back in for more.

It might not look like a Hoyoverse game, but there's one thing Nodusfall certainly does look like. Namely Elden Ring , and by extension, its co-op sibling Nightreign . This doesn't end with its reveal trailer vibes – we have a summonable Torrent-like steed who can be called with a very familiar-sounding whistle, a character who can transform into a phase two Malenia lookalike with massive, crusty wings, Estus flask-like healing potions, and bonfires to rest at.

Developer: MiHoYo Platfom(s): PC Release date: TBC

Needless to say, it's hard not to draw comparisons – 'we've got Elden Ring Nightreign at home,' my brain screams. However, while teaming up with other players to take down big bosses might evoke feelings of FromSoftware 's co-op title, there's a big difference with Nodusfall: it's not nearly as hard. This can be considered a blessing or a curse depending on where you stand on Soulslike difficulty. As a fan of the genre, I still found myself having plenty of fun taking down the three bosses in my hands-on session, including an enormous dragon and Qiongqi (a horned and winged tiger-like beast from Chinese mythology), but my victories definitely didn't come with the same level of satisfaction as they might have had they been slightly harder won. I can't recall falling in battle even once, largely thanks to what felt like an unlimited supply of heals.

To be fair, this factor may also have been helped by one of the playable characters being a dedicated healer, who I choose to play in my session. I have strong magic attacks up my sleeve, from small projectiles to ice-powered strikes and an enormous laser beam move, but my main contribution to my team comes in the form of my healing abilities. I can choose to lock onto a specific ally to unleash a steady flow of health restoration, not unlike Mercy's Caduceus staff in Overwatch, or heal multiple teammates around me at once in a smaller burst.

The specific ally lock-on heal can feel a little clunky at times – there were more than a few times where I assisted someone who definitely didn't need it because they were awkwardly stood in front of someone else who desperately needed my help. Comparing directly to Elden Ring Nightreign, though, it's really cool to have a healer option in the first place. Again, it seems that Nodusfall doesn't come close to being as challenging as FromSoftware's Soulslikes to begin with, but having a medic role like this is no doubt going to provide a welcome option to players who aren't as comfortable with getting up close and personal on the frontlines of a brutal battle. I always tend to gravitate towards support classes in games – there's just something so satisfying about keeping your friends and allies going – so I'm pleased to be allowed that here.

Nodusfall looks more like Monster Hunter and Elden Ring than games from Genshin Impact's Hoyoverse Nodusfall isn't a gacha game, Mihoyo confirms Mihoyo CEO says Monster Hunter-like Nodusfall is very "un-Mihoyo," which hopefully means less gacha I'd have been curious to try out the other playable characters to get a greater feel for Nodusfall's combat. What I experienced was fun, but my attacks felt like they were lacking weight, leaving me craving just a tad more oomph. You really can't fault the boss battles when it comes to how cinematic they are, though – my team and I tore through multiple phases in each fight, with our final battle against the Maldrake dragon evolving after the knight riding on its back dismounted their steed and began attacking us from the ground, forcing us to split our forces to take on two enemies at once.

The concept of an easier, more accessible co-op action game like Nightreign is bound to be appealing

Though my Nodusfall experience was limited to co-op PvE, Hoyoverse has clarified that PvP and PvPvE modes are also planned for the long term, and that you'll also be able to enjoy most of the core content solo. From what I played, though, it'd be a shame to do so since you'd miss out on the flashy Joint Execution moves – who doesn't want to team up to drive a massive greatsword through a beast's head?

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

I was also pleased to learn that, despite plans to make Nodusfall a free-to-play game, playable characters won't be locked behind a gacha system. With that said, the devs are considering monetizing cosmetics, and I can't say I'm surprised. While kitting out my healer girl with a new outfit, various accessories including a fancy, glowing cape were screaming microtransaction potential. I can't say I love that aspect, but I'd certainly much rather the monetization be incorporated here than the core gameplay.

As someone who loved Elden Ring Nightreign, I suppose it's only natural that I'd enjoy Nodusfall. Its vibe is very similar, but I'm very curious to see where Hoyoverse takes it from here. The concept of an easier, more accessible co-op action game like Nightreign is bound to be appealing to many, and could be a bridge for those who find FromSoftware's games a bit too difficult. Regardless, there's something in here that's got me craving more – but for now, I guess I've literally got Nightreign at home.

Quick Review: ELDEN RING TARNISHED EDITION (Switch 2)
items.summary: Story and Gameplay We got our review copy a bit late but wanted to share our quick thoughts on the the highly anticipated Switch 2 edition of ELDEN RING. This is an absolute modern classic, and there
items.content:
We got our review copy a bit late but wanted to share our quick thoughts on the the highly anticipated Switch 2 edition of ELDEN RING. This is an absolute modern classic, and there's not much to say that we didn't cover in our original review beyond reminding everyone, Soulslike fan or not, that this game deserves to be played on any platform. The Switch 2 version isn't perfect, but it's extremely well done. The Tarnished Edition content is welcome, though not a game-changer by any means. New starting classes, new armor, etc. are a nice touch, but it's the base game that remains one of the best ever made.

The audiovisual presentation is stunning whether you're playing in handheld mode or docked. I just wish more Switch 2 ports had a performance mode option to reduce graphical fidelity and try to hit 50 or 60 fps. Either way, this Switch 2 port is definitely polished and I’m glad we got a solid and smooth version of this gem.

The soundtrack and sound effects remain some of the best in the industry. No complaints here and fans will be pleased at this sonic landscape.

At $79.99 MSRP, the price is a bit of a mystery, since the original game was $59.99. Yes, the DLC and new content are included, but it still feels like a big asking price and knocks our score down a bit. Beyond that and the performance mode option I wish were here, there's little to complain about.

The Switch 2 version of ELDEN RING is finally upon us, and whether you've played it to death before or never touched it, this version rocks and I highly recommend it. Playing through it again reminded me how much I love this masterpiece and FromSoftware in general. Every Switch 2 owner deserves to have this in their library, even if they have to wait for an eventual (maybe) sale.

items.title: Four Years Later, Players Are Still Falling For Elden Ring’s Biggest Trick
items.summary: New Elden Ring players are swiftly being transported to Sellia Crystal Tunnel and learning about the game the hard way.
items.content:
Four Years Later, Players Are Still Falling For Elden Ring’s Biggest Trick From TheGamer (Written by Sam Woods) on September 1, 2026 | OpenCritic

Elden Ring is made by FromSoftware. FromSoftware makes notoriously difficult video games. Therefore, in conclusion, Elden Ring is a difficult video game. This is something many of us have found out by now, with the masterpiece having been released over four and a half years ago.

However, good games never die, and with Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition now releasing on the Nintendo Switch 2, a whole new audience is experiencing the game. It also means a whole new audience is experiencing the trials and tribulations that come with it. One of these, which many of us are all too familiar with, is the Teleporter Trap in the Dragon Burnt Ruins, something that new players are encountering for the first time, with hilarious consequences.

Elden Ring is FromSoftware's first big open-world game. The way the map is laid out, however, means players are likely to gravitate towards the Dragon Burnt Ruins pretty early on in their adventures. It's a grand introduction to the game's mechanics, enemies, and structure, but it has one little caveat — a Teleporter Trap that will transport you into the far more dangerous Sellia Crystal Tunnel .

It's a trap that's easy to fall into, simply by opening...

Knight Leontiel and Noble Broken Mask were both added to the game as part of Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition DLC.

Watch On Knight Leontiel is a straight "hey, I know them" reference to Lucatiel of Mirrah from Dark Souls 2, boasting an HD remaster of her signature conquistador fit and nimble greatsword. Take off the mask, though, and Leontiel practically is Lucatiel, even down to a burn mark over her left eye that corresponds to the hollowing rot Lucatiel suffered in Dark Souls 2.

Noble Broken Mask, meanwhile, may obliquely give us a better idea of what his base game counterpart and spiritual rival, Goldmask, is supposed to look like. Goldmask's model has a face, but it seems like a generic placeholder element. Broken Mask has an austere, pinched face with striking pale gold eyes, and Zullie points out that he bears a more than passing resemblance to the typically obscured faces of Elden Ring 's perfumer enemies.

Zullie provides character creation slider information for the two so you can perfectly recreate either one as your own guy⁠—most FromSoft NPCs are made using the same tools available to players. This is not the first time Zullie has done this: She has previously made videos zooming in on Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree's NPCs . All the way back in 2016, she did the same for Dark Souls 3's cast .

Even with everything coming out right now, it's kind of a great time to revisit Elden Ring thanks to the Tarnished Edition. Even if you don't shell out for the new stuff, the servers will be more populated for the next few weeks than they likely ever will be again. And if you need help finding the new Tarnished Edition gear , PCG guides writer Sean Martin has got you covered.

items.title: Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition is exciting enough on its own, but it's also our last chance to properly experience the game's launch day hype
items.content:
One last hurrah for "fort comma night," "Mist, or Beast," and "offer pickle."

You can subscribe to the newsletter at the link if you want to get our thoughts about a new videogame happening direct to your inbox every Thursday.

Elden Ring is one of the best videogames I've ever played, and now, four years from launch, is possibly the last time you'll get to experience it as an event . The Tarnished Edition DLC looks small on paper⁠—two new classes and a smattering of armor and items⁠—but it is still something new, something unexpected added to our 2022 game of the year.

What in any other context might make for a Horse Armor -style embarrassment is one of the most exciting releases of 2026 for me, and I'm only, like, a quarter joking. Elden Ring is the type of game that made a couple borked quests getting patched into a massive communal treasure hunt . New weapons, armor, and classes at this late date feels like a profound gift, even if I'm paying for the privilege.

But, in addition to the material additions coming to Elden Ring, the Tarnished Edition DLC serves as an enticement to the playerbase, something to bring them back all at one time and bring life back to the Lands Between's ailing multiplayer invasions and co-operative boss battling.

I still remember how magical the first days of Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree were, the density of asynchronous messages and ease of matchmaking. The Tarnished Edition won't be able to match either of those highs, but its launch may represent the biggest spike in player activity we could ever expect to see in Elden Ring again.

If you've somehow missed the boat on this one since 2022, I envy the first experience you're about to have. Elden Ring's fantasy is somehow both mythic and anthropological, zoomed out, and deeply personal.

Elden Ring players are hard at work putting the new Tarnished Edition DLC's gear to the test Where to find new armor and weapons in Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition This action RPG's more-with-more-on-top excess is as fun as expansion design gets

You're an anonymous warrior on a quest to become God's Husband (gender-agnostic). The God in question is a man and woman, separate but the same, consubstantial with, and plotting against themselves. Her pope is a giant turtle , and she is perpetuating a millennia-old conflict involving both racial animus and metaphysics. You can make her goth half- (single? step?) daughter God instead if you so choose.

It's all set in a world of literally impossible beauty, one of the best fantasy settings ever rendered in a videogame. It's dominated by the alien, iconic view of the Erdtree, an ethereal, skyscraper-sized growth that's visible from every part of the Lands Between. Elden Ring is, perhaps, one of FromSoftware 's most bright and cheerful creations to date, but it's also one of the weirdest. In four years, it's lodged itself into my psyche like almost no game world I've ever seen.

But enough about all that nerd stuff: FromSoft had already ruined all other 3D action games for me by the time Elden Ring came out, and while it lacks the pure focus of Sekiro's perfect block symphony , I think it matches that more straightforward action game as a fantasy combat experience. Elden Ring is one of the broadest, deepest, and most exquisitely designed action-RPGs that's ever been made.

It even contains Sekiro in a limited sense: One of the character build options added in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is a perfect block mechanic lifted straight out of the ninja sim. Like no other game I've played, Elden Ring balances mechanically pure "it's your fault if you die" combat with a myriad of class fantasies and character build options. Knights, barbarians, spellcasters, rogues, priests, samurai, nude men with earthenware hats, you can inhabit any of these roles while engaging in some of the tightest, richest, and most challenging action combat put to silicon.

items.title: 'Elden Ring' Fans Just Got a Major Reason to Come Back to the Game
items.summary: 'Elden Ring' is getting a huge new patch that adds new weapons and rebalances several items.
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Elijah Gonzalez Published Aug 27, 2026, 12:25 PM EDT News Elden Ring is getting a big new patch alongside the Switch 2's Tarnished Edition

Image: FromSoftware/Bandai Namco Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 3 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Elden Ring Tarnished Edition , which bundles the base game and its excellent Shadow of the Erdtree DLC alongside some new additions, is finally coming to Nintendo Switch 2 this week. As part of its release, Elden Ring is getting a major new patch across all systems , with the new weapons and armor added with the Switch 2 edition of the game for sale as the “Tarnished Pack” DLC.

Tarnished Edition includes two new starting classes, new weapons that can be found or purchased from merchants, and three new attire options for the spectral steed Torrent. Other additions include new invasion events in Caelid and Leyndell, including one where a devout, mostly naked man attacks you with a flail. The DLC will be available on all systems on Aug. 28, the same day the Switch 2 releases.

However, even those who don’t pay for this new content will find a long list of balance changes and other updates. For starters, from now on, certain powerful enemies in the Realm of Shadow will drop higher-tier items and treasures. Numerous weapons received buffs, including Rellana’s Twin Blades and Spear of the Impaler, while several shields received better guard boost (what percent of incoming damage is blocked) and reduced weight​​​. Perfume Bottle enjoyers will be pleased to find attack power increases that may make this tool less niche. Several underused sorceries and incantations also received improvements. The only nerf in PvE was to Rakshasa’s Great Katana, which now has a greater delay to right-hand attacks after attacking with a left-hand weapon.

One of the biggest potential changes is that parries have been enhanced across the board, with “improved parry performance.” Presumably, this means a larger parry window or faster activation. There were also a handful of PvP nerfs where Rakshasa’s Great Katana got hit again, as well as a few incantations.

The critical response to Elden Ring Tarnished Edition on the Switch 2 has been quite positive, with critics impressed by how well the game runs on the handheld. This version was originally planned for 2025 but was delayed so the team could optimize the game’s performance after a rough showing at last year's Gamescom .

items.title: I Tested Elden Ring On Switch 2 In A Cozy Cafe And It Ran Just Fine, Which Is Great News For A Remarkable Game
items.summary: You shouldn't play it in the rain/but you can play it on a train
items.content:
Elden Ring is an excellent, excellent video game. It’s got that smashy FromSoftware combat, a couple hundred boss fights that are all (mostly) unique and fun, character build customization for miles, a gorgeous and massive open world that’s a treat to explore, an intriguing story and hidden secrets, and a robust DLC that could be a game all its own. There’s a reason (well, many reasons!) why it’s almost universally critically acclaimed and still beloved by fans a few years after launch, too.

I love Elden Ring ! But when Ethan asked me to take on the review of the Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2, I wasn’t, like, stoked about it. I beat Elden Ring back when it first came out, easily dumping over 100 hours into the main game and probably another solid 40 or more into the DLC. And I played the Tarnished Edition at a preview event earlier this year for about 20 minutes, after which time I told everyone I spoke with about the experience that yup, that was Elden Ring all right! Elden Ring on a Switch 2! Game’s great, but I don’t necessarily need to play it again. What else is there to say?

It turns out, after playing for review, I do have one additional thing to say: Elden Ring is, apparently, pretty fun to play in public. Ideally at a cozy coffee shop with squoshy chairs where you can purchase hot London fogs to drink while you play.

Elden Ring was technically playable on the go before the Tarnished Edition , for folks with a Steam Deck. I have one of those, but the device, unlike the Switch 2, is not fun to take out in public. It’s heavy to hold, does not have a convenient kickstand, and you have to hold it in your hands to play if you don’t want to drag a controller around too. With the Switch 2, I could set the console on the table with the kickstand out, take the Joy-Cons off, lean back in my chair, and play Elden Ring while soothing cafe music played in the background. Every time I die (which is often), I get a nice sip of tea. I do not rage. I do not tense up. Helpfully, the cat (who is not here in the cafe with me) does not butt her head against the triggers and cause me to swing my sword randomly. Life is good.

In basically every other respect, I stick to my guns from the preview: this is Elden Ring ! It’s on the Switch 2 now! There were concerns after the first round of early previews that it ran poorly, but those were fixed by the time I previewed it earlier this year and remain fixed now. It runs fine. There are still occasional little framerate drops and yeah, it doesn’t look quite as nice as it will on your PS5 or Xbox Series, but who cares? It still plays great. The minor technical compromises didn’t interfere with combat in any way that was meaningful to me. It still looks good. It’s still lovely to stand on a cliff’s edge and look out in the direction of the Erdtree, the sun’s rays glistening through the clouds and a skyline of crumbling ruin all around.

I should mention that the Tarnished Edition does not have any meaningful new features. There are four new armor sets, a bit of customization for Torrent, and two new starting classes. Unfortunately, two of those new armor sets are starting sets for the two new classes, Heavy Knight and Idus Knight. I played as the Idus Knight and replaced my armor almost immediately with some tunic thing I got off a knight in the very first part of Limgrave, because it had better stats. I think I wore this same tunic when I played the game the first time. Shame, because the new starting armor genuinely looked great. I found the addition of these two new classes to be extremely whatever: you’re going to customize all your stats and replace all your gear almost immediately anyway. The Idus Knight was just a Samurai two levels lower, with different equipment. These additions did nothing for me, and certainly will do nothing for anyone after the first hour of game.

This release does include the superb Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, bundled right in from the start, though. That rules.

But who cares? It’s Elden Ring , on Switch 2! I can easily play it on a plane or on a train, in a box or with a fox, here or there, anywhere! I can take it to bars, to rooftop wine parties. I can play it outside on a patio with a cold one in a koozie next to me as the summer sun sets. I recognize that this is just effectively restating the main gimmick of the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2, but I admittedly haven’t taken my Switch 2 out much since it launched last year. Elden Ring , the best game of 2022 and arguably one of the best games of the decade, is a great excuse to do so. Give it a shot. Order yourself a latte or, a little later in the day, maybe a nice glass of pinot noir, bust out your Switch 2, and give it a shot.

This article was corrected post-publication: Limveld is Nightreign , Limgrave is Elden Ring . I can never keep them straight.

items.title: Elden Ring plays much better than I'd expected on Switch 2, but it isn't without its flaws
items.summary: The power of the Nintendo Switch 2 definitely knows its bounds, but that hasn't stopped Nintendo and co. from taking on this ambitious Elden Ring Switch 2 port.
items.content:
Image credit: FromSoftware/Eurogamer Feature by Kelsey Raynor Senior Guides Writer Published on Aug. 26, 2026, 2 p.m. 37 comments Follow Elden Ring Prioritise us on Google The power of the Nintendo Switch 2 definitely knows its bounds, but that hasn't stopped Nintendo and its fellow publishers from trying to push the handheld device to its limits by porting some of the more demanding and gargantuan of games to the console. The release of Elden Ring : Tarnished Edition is one example of that ambition. I've only been able to spend about ten hours with it so far, which saw me clearing out Weeping Peninsula, Stormveil Castle, and Liurnia of the Lakes before moving onto the treacherous place that is Caelid. This means I'm yet to explore the portion of the game whose performance I'm most curious about – the DLC's Realm of Shadow – but more on that shortly. (This is your spoiler warning for the DLC's ending, as I'll be discussing that below.)

First things first, one thing that Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition proved to me (again) is that stepping foot into The Lands Between will never grow old, even when you find yourself stumbling along in 30 FPS and waiting around for slightly longer loading screens. Now, if you've never played Elden Ring before and this is your first foray into the game, 30 FPS won't necessarily be the shock to you that it was to me. I'm very much used to playing Elden Ring on my PC with my Xbox controller at a stable 60 FPS, so my first real enemy encounter this time around was the 'thick air' of The Lands Between, as well as the Switch 2's button inputs. Pressing 'A' to dodge and 'X' to interact (rather than 'B' and 'Y' respectively), despite these buttons being in the same positions on the Switch 2's Joy-Cons, felt alien to me at first. Alas, this is nothing you shouldn't be expecting, and nothing you can't quickly get used to in my experience.

By the time I reached Stormveil and took down the game's first two bosses, Margit and Godrick, my focus on the FPS had long felt like something of the past. I'd got used to dodging a little earlier than I normally would, and charging my heavy attacks the slightest bit further ahead of time. Aside from the few frame drops I experienced while sprinting through Liurnia of the Lakes to track down the Academy Glintstone Key, I was pleasantly surprised that Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition played as well as it did, while also looking near-enough as wonderful as it did on my PC. Simply put, once you're used to how thick the air feels at lower FPS, the Tarnished Edition otherwise runs as smoothly as you'd hope in docked mode. For the most part.

The first issues I encountered were with the Red Wolf of Radagon, who is your first boss in Liurnia of the Lakes, and most players' third boss in the whole game if you're following the critical path. This is an incredibly agile wolf who jumps and lunges around the room, snapping at you with its jaws and swiping at you with a magical sword it's able to conjure. This is also one of the first arguably 'fast' bosses you'll fight, and it was during this encounter that things first began to falter. Dodging its lunges and swipes wasn't an issue for the most part, but on more occasions than I'd like – usually when the Red Wolf was slinging its magical sword around – I'd experience frame drops so damning that it was any wonder I survived some of them. Ultimately, I ended up fighting the beast with the ol' trusty Reduvia Dagger's ranged weapon art, so I could keep a safe distance. Rennala, the boss who immediately follows Red Wolf of Radagon, was – like Margit and Godrick – a very smooth fight however.

All in all, this one experience did put a sour taste in my mouth. I plan on seeing Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition through to the very end, as it's been a long time since I replayed the game with an entirely new character. The Tarnished Edition also introduces two new Starting Classes that incentivise this, one of which includes a new Light Greatsword (which happens to be our second standard Light Greatsword in the whole game, which I'm pleased to see). In spite of my excitement though, I do fear for how later bosses will play out. Especially those in the DLC, such as Divine Beast Dancing Lion and Messmer the Impaler. Given that my PC sometimes struggled with frame drops during the former, and the latter is one of the fastest bosses in the game, I do wonder how these will go down on the Nintendo Switch 2 if Red Wolf of Radagon was the first boss to falter.

Above all that though, my biggest concern lies with the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC's final boss, Promised Consort Radahn. Not only the toughest fight conjured up by FromSoftware to date (in my opinion), this fight doesn't just test your skills, but it also will test your gaming rig. Given that I struggled with this fight from both a difficulty perspective and because my PC couldn't keep up with all the Gravity attacks being hurled at me, I really do wonder just how well the Nintendo Switch 2 will hold up during this fight, and during the ones that lead up to it. Time will only tell as myself and other players foray through The Lands Between and into the Realm of Shadow once more. My hope is that the rather promising start I've had – Red Wolf of Radagon issues aside – holds up as we all progress with our adventure to become Elden Lord all over again.

While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression.

Watch On From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great!

Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. In the reveal trailer embedded above, I saw giant bears, some sort of giant pack foxes, a horned, winged manticore, and a dragon or two (giant). I don't yet know how Nodusfall's progression works, but if I'm not allowed to harvest all their individual pieces and turn them into pants, I'm going to feel personally betrayed.

While the glimpses of combat shown in the footage looks like it hews pretty closely to the pace and rhythm of Monster Hunter, Nodusfall does seem to be dropping a few original elements into the mix. At one point, one of the player characters uses some sort of transformation ability to become a giant, armored knight in the middle of a hunt. And later, two players perform an elaborate, paired execution animation.

Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' All the key details on HoYo's co-op monster slayer Nodusfall What remains to be seen is what sort of monetization scheme Nodusfall will be wrapped in—something that HoYoverse's history doesn't exactly inspire confidence about. If I have to do gacha pulls for a gunlance, I'm going to have a hard time.

Nodusfall doesn't have much of an online presence yet, so it'll likely be a while before we can expect a release date.

items.title: Miyazaki suggests FromSoftware is keen to return to single-player games after The Duskbloods and Elden Ring: Nightreign
items.summary: Souls house FromSoftware has done back-to-back multiplayer games with The Duskbloods and Elden Ring: Nightreign. But it hasn't forgotten solo players.
items.content:
Image credit: Eurogamer/FromSoftware News by Robert Purchese Associate Editor Published on Aug. 20, 2026, 4:44 p.m. 37 comments Follow The Duskbloods Prioritise us on Google Hidetaka Miyazaki , the president of FromSoftware and director of so many revered Soulsian games, has suggested the studio is keen to return to making single-player games after The Duskbloods.

Speaking to IGN , Miyazaki explained it was a coincidence that 2025's Elden Ring: Nightreign and The Duskbloods were both multiplayer games. "It's funny because there was never really any big plan that these two games [Nightreign and The Duskbloods] would both release next to each other," he said.

"I mean, that's a different director," he added, referring to Junya Ishizaki who helmed Nightreign, "but both of those ideas just coincided with being multiplayer games. It's not necessarily some big reveal saying that this is the direction we plan to go moving forward. We still have a heavy focus on single-player content as well. This is just something that happened to work out the way it did."

It was while continuing this thought, and saying it had been fun to make a multiplayer game, that Miyazaki said: "But it's like, the more you work on something multiplayer for a long time, if anything, it scratches that itch only to want to make something single-player again."

FromSoftware's last big single-player game was 2022's barnstorming Elden Ring , which included a more traditional form of multiplayer for the studio - including co-op and invasions. But Elden Ring didn't showcase multiplayer in the way Nightreign did or that Switch 2 exclusive The Duskbloods will - with a much more actively competitive multiplayer PvPvE experience.

Indeed, it seems as though it's The Duskbloods that's the anomaly for FromSoftware, with Miyazaki describing it as an outlet for ideas that "didn't really fit in the context of a single-player game".

"Over time," he said, "a lot of those ideas piled up, things that you wish you could have done here and there. Having an outlet for them, somewhere we can find a place where they all fit, or can be made to fit specifically in that multiplayer context, is something that was always at the forefront of my mind."

The Duskbloods is a Switch 2 exclusive made in partnership with Nintendo. Miyazaki said this relationship came about from a mixture of Nintendo being "very excited and very receptive to the idea" of The Duskbloods, and "very forward thinking in terms of how to do it". Nintendo's input can be felt in the game, as well, particularly in how it helps ease players in..

"The onboarding tutorials and making sure players understand how the game works and how to succeed in the game is something we've historically not been super great at conveying instantly," Miyazaki said. "We've definitely just dropped players in and hoped they would figure it out. In this case, Nintendo is definitely the right partner for better conveying that information in a way that is understandable to the player; it definitely suits their strengths."

This weekend's The Duskbloods network test runs in five phases , one each day from 21st August (Friday) through to 24th August (Monday). The full game has no release date yet, despite a 24th September date appearing briefly today , but FromSoftware has previously committed to it coming out this year . The pertinent question this autumn is: how close to GTA 6 's 19th November release dare it go?

items.title: Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching Aug. 28 on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Pre-order available. Explore a breathtaking world full of excitement and mystery.
items.content:
08/11/26 Pre-order now Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching Aug. 28 on Nintendo Switch 2 The Lands Between—a place of myth, gods, and broken dreams. Long ago, Queen Marika and her divine offspring reigned here, but since the Elden Ring was shattered, the world has fallen into decay. Now, the land whispers for a King.

The “Tarnished,” long exiled, are finally seeing the light of Grace once more. Step into this hauntingly beautiful realm, unravel its ancient mysteries, and rise as the one true Elden Lord.

The ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition game arrives on the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system on August 28 .

The Lands Between are part of a vast continent, where magnificent open fields and huge dungeons with complex three-dimensional designs are seamlessly connected. As you explore, the joy of discovering unknown and overwhelming threats awaits you.

Mastery of the terrain and knowledge of its secrets can help you overcome enemies and defeat formidable bosses—or lead invading players into traps.

The founding mythology of Elden Ring was written by George R. R. Martin and adapted into a rich multilayered story. Intersecting goals and desires between the characters create an intense narrative that weaves throughout the Lands Between. The events of the game can unravel in many ways—depending on your interventions.

Combat is simple to learn yet offers hidden depths of dexterity. As you seek to become the Elden Lord, you’ll need to explore the balance between attacking, avoiding damage, using a wide variety of weapons, spells, summons, and perfecting your timing to take advantage of your opponents’ weaknesses.

In addition to customizing the appearance of your character, there are countless ways to combine the weapons, armor, usable items, and magic that you equip. You can develop your character according to your play style.

No matter if you prefer bold physical confrontation, tactical spellcasting, or the subtle art of stealth, you’ll be able to find gear that supports your choices.

Traverse together with other Nintendo Switch 2 players. You can play with up to two other Tarnished as your cooperative teammates, either by inviting them using a shared password or by summoning them from a pool of nearby community members.

There are also ample opportunities to face off against other players, either through co-op invasions, invited duels, or the many player battle options available in the three Colosseums.

If you’d like to learn more or begin your journey to the Lands Between by pre-ordering the Tarnished Edition, please check out the link below.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

A Collector’s Treasure

items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.
